params.body:
The Gentells app for Android signs a member in the way the Observatory does: gentells.com in Chrome's Auth Tab, the Observatory's first-party OAuth client with PKCE, then the pipeline's `POST /auth/site` for the session. The pipeline needs no change. This site needs one more redirect for that client, and a file that names the app.

## What changes

- **`gentells:observatory-client` takes every redirect the client answers**, here the Observatory's callback and `https://gentells.com/app/callback`. It keeps exactly the ones given, and still refuses anything that is not http(s).
- **`/.well-known/assetlinks.json`** lists the builds in `ANDROID_APPS` (`package=SHA-256 of the signing certificate`, comma separated). Malformed entries are dropped, and the list is empty until a build is named.
- **`/app/callback`** is a page for the case where Android did not hand the address to the app (a build that is not named, or a computer). It tells the reader to open the app and sign in again. The code in the address is useless without the verifier the app kept.
- Both routes answer behind the holding page (`PreLaunch`).
- `docs/design/android-app.md` describes the flow and the two settings.

## Why an https address and not a scheme of the app's own

The Observatory's client skips the consent screen (`OAuthClient::skipsAuthorization`). With a private-use scheme such as `com.gentells.app:/oauth/callback`, any app that registers the same scheme could start its own sign-in, and a reader already signed in on gentells.com would be signed in to that app without seeing anything (RFC 8252, section 8.6). PKCE does not stop this, because that app holds its own verifier. Android hands an https address on gentells.com only to the app that `assetlinks.json` names by its certificate. That is also why the command refuses non-http(s) redirects; a test covers three spellings of a claimable scheme.

The address stays on this origin, which also keeps the redirect chain after a password login inside the site's `form-action 'self'`.

## After merge

1. In the site's environment: `ANDROID_APPS="com.gentells.app.preview=8C:E8:9F:CC:A7:62:DE:E4:6B:3D:53:91:31:BC:C0:1D:4D:7E:48:17:1C:8C:63:F7:92:C6:16:75:73:50:DE:51"` (the preview build's development key).
2. On the box: `php artisan gentells:observatory-client https://observatory.gentells.com/auth/callback https://gentells.com/app/callback`. Name both, because the client keeps only what is given.

Until step 2 the Observatory's web login is unchanged. Until step 1 the app cannot sign in.

## Checked

- `AndroidAppTest` 7/7:
  - the client keeps its redirects and only those;
  - a claimable scheme is refused and changes nothing;
  - the whole authorize and token exchange with the app's redirect, with no consent screen;
  - an unlisted redirect gets no code;
  - `assetlinks.json` contents, and both routes behind the holding page.
- Mutations caught: no scheme check, only the first redirect kept, the callback behind the cover, the fingerprint pattern, the relation.
- Full suite 528/529. `BuildStampTest` fails in any worktree because the branch ref lives in the common git dir.
- Pint and `bin/lint-tailwind` pass.
params.title: Let the Gentells app sign in with the Observatory's client
